ai.literal: Goddess is it, beautiful peacock is it, heavy-earringed woman is it? Is confused my heart.
ai.translation: Is she a goddess, a beautiful peacock, or a mortal woman wearing heavy earrings? My heart is utterly bewildered.
ai.modern: இவள் தெய்வப் பெண்ணா, அல்லது அழகிய மயிலா, அல்லது கனமான காதணிகளை அணிந்த மனிதப் பெண்ணா என்று தெரியாமல் என் நெஞ்சம் மயங்குகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet captures the speaker's overwhelming awe upon seeing a beautiful woman for the first time. He wonders if she is a celestial goddess, a graceful peacock, or a mortal woman adorned with heavy earrings. The repeated use of the particle 'kol' (is it / or) emphasizes his deep uncertainty and wonder. Ultimately, her stunning appearance leaves his heart completely bewildered and unable to decide.

ai.translation: When she returns my look with a glance of her own, it is like an attacking spirit bringing an army with it.

ai.explanation: The speaker describes the overwhelming effect of the woman returning his gaze. He compares her natural beauty to a spirit that already has the power to attack and afflict him. When she actively looks back at him, it multiplies her power, as if that attacking spirit has now armed itself with an entire army.

ai.literal: Formerly I knew not Death, that which is called; now I have known (it), with womanly beauty it has eyes of great battle.
ai.translation: I never knew what Death was before, but now I know: it takes the form of a beautiful woman with large, battling eyes.
ai.modern: முன்பு எமன் என்று சொல்லப்படுவதை நான் அறிந்ததில்லை; ஆனால் இப்போது அறிந்தேன், அது பெண் தன்மையுடன் பெரிய போர் செய்யும் கண்களை உடையது என்று.
ai.explanation: The speaker, struck by the heroine's beauty, compares her captivating eyes to Death itself. He says that he had only heard of Death before but had never seen it. Now he realizes that Death does not come as a terrifying figure, but rather wrapped in feminine beauty, armed with large, piercing eyes that wage a battle on his heart.

ai.literal: Death? Eye? Doe? Innocent woman's look these all three possesses.
ai.translation: Is it Death, an eye, or a timid doe? The look of this innocent woman has the nature of all three.

ai.explanation: The speaker is captivated and bewildered by the woman's glance. He wonders if what he sees is Death, a mere eye, or a timid doe. He concludes that the look of this innocent woman possesses the qualities of all three: the deadliness of Death, the natural form of an eye, and the captivating, startled beauty of a doe. The repeated particle 'o' expresses his intense doubt and wonder.

ai.literal: Curved eyebrows having bent if hide, trembling sorrow will not cause indeed this woman's eyes.
ai.translation: If her curved eyebrows would bend and conceal them, this woman's eyes would not cause me such trembling sorrow.
ai.modern: இவளுடைய வளைந்த புருவங்கள் கீழ்நோக்கி வளைந்து கண்களை மறைக்குமானால், இவளது கண்கள் எனக்கு இந்த நடுங்கும் துன்பத்தை தரமாட்டா.
ai.explanation: The speaker is captivated and overwhelmed by the woman's gaze. He notes that her eyes inflict a shivering distress upon him, which could only be stopped if her curved eyebrows bent down to hide them. The word 'கோடா' is used here in the classical pattern of a positive adverbial participle meaning 'having bent', showing how her downward glance might spare him from the direct strike of her eyes.

ai.literal: To the bright forehead, oh!, it broke indeed, in battle even foes fear, my pride.
ai.translation: My great pride, which terrifies even my enemies on the battlefield, has shattered before her bright forehead. Oh!
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் பகைவரும் கண்டு அஞ்சுகின்ற என்னுடைய வீரப்பெருமை, இவளுடைய ஒளிபொருந்திய நெற்றியைக் கண்டதும் உடைந்துவிட்டதே!
ai.explanation: The hero marvels at the overwhelming power of the heroine's beauty. He is a fierce warrior whose strength and pride ('பீடு') strike terror into his enemies on the battlefield ('ஞாட்பு'). Yet, that very same unshakeable pride has completely shattered before her radiant forehead ('ஒண்ணுதல்'). The exclamation 'ஓஒ' expresses his helpless astonishment at how easily love has conquered his martial valor.

ai.literal: With those who drank except, brewed liquor, love like, those who saw joy causing is not.
ai.translation: Brewed liquor brings joy only to those who drink it. Unlike love, it cannot intoxicate those who merely look at it.
ai.modern: காய்ச்சப்பட்ட மது தன்னை உண்டவர்களுக்கு மட்டுமே மகிழ்ச்சி தரும். ஆனால் காதல், மதுவைப் போலன்றி, பார்த்த அளவிலேயே மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தரக்கூடியது.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the intoxicating effects of liquor with the power of love. The phrase 'அடுநறா' refers to strong, brewed liquor, which only affects the person who actually consumes it. Love, however, is far more potent. Unlike liquor, love can intoxicate and bring immense joy to a person just by the mere sight of the beloved.
